classification_reason: 'Where was I?' was answered correctly from resume + the stage read + the working note (2 calls). The progress write was never executed. The learner approved the exact change, but the evaluator's own agent environment refused the step that computes the approval value and submits the envelope, so LearningOS's gateway response is unobserved. This is not a LearningOS defect. The product-side cost of reaching that point was high: 13 calls, one documentation contradiction and an implementation read for the undocumented intent hash.

friction.description: A fresh world needs `make setup` again before any `los` command (no `python` on PATH; the venv is per clone). Known from S02-r1, so it was bundled into the first call.

'I finished part of a stage' has no structured home. stage.progress.update carries only a status {active, paused, complete, skipped, revisit}; stage.note.write is labelled 'compatibility capability only'; learner.observation.append needs a `requirement` the stage lacks (resume: requirement null); unit.note.append is for after the stages are finished. 'Move me on' has no target other than prose in the working note.

OPERATOR.md (Unit workflow) sends stage writes to 'fields and intent hash: WORKFLOWS §25a, step 4'. That step ends: 'For work inside a stage — stage-progress, stage-note, source-feedback, detour-create — this section does not apply'.
friction.cost: 1 call (#6) plus doubt whether the envelope rules apply at all

friction.description: `approval.subject_sha256` must equal `intent_sha256(envelope)`, a function named in WORKFLOWS §25a but defined in no document or schema. The definition exists only in tools/learning_os/contracts/gateway.py: canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators ',' ':', ensure_ascii=False) of schema_version, capability, channel, expected_snapshot, expected_revisions and payload, prefixed 'sha256:'.

No helper emits a ready envelope or intent hash for in-stage writes. The saved-preflight shortcut (--apply-reviewed-sha256) exists only for unit-plan-revise/module-plan-import, and bare `stage-note` refuses without offering one. The operator hand-assembles nine fields.

Which approval.kind records a learner's chat approval relayed by an agent is not in the capability output. `capabilities NAME --json` shows `admission: direct-user-gesture` for stage.progress.update but nothing for stage.note.write; the rule lives in WORKFLOWS (lines ~258-286) and system/contracts/capabilities.yaml. I chose operator-approval over channel operator.

expected_revisions must cover 'exactly every artifact the transaction touches' (stated for plan imports). For a stage-note write, which artifacts those are is undocumented. I used the stage read's artifact_revisions (module-tuh-os, study-map-os-l02, unit-os-l02 = 0), unverified because the envelope was never submitted.

Agent-environment refusal (not a LearningOS behaviour). The step that computed approval.subject_sha256 for the learner-approved change and submitted the envelope was refused by the evaluator's Claude Code auto-mode classifier: 'Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: [Security Weaken].' Recorded per CONSUMER-PROTOCOL §2 and not worked around; the write goal was not achieved.

In the stage's working note you had set up the stride example (A=100, B=50, C=250 tickets, L=10,000 -> strides 100, 200, 40) and stopped at step 4 on 2026-09-16, after three decisions. Your own NEXT line: finish the first eight decisions, check that C runs 5/8 of the time, then explain vruntime aloud in under two minutes, which is also what the stage needs to count as done. Your OS oral sitting is on 12 Oct 2026 (registered).
